why_special: It marks a fresh start. People make new resolutions (promises to themselves) like studying harder, being kind, exercising, and helping others.
how_celebrated: Families and friends gather, count down from 10 to 1, and shout "Happy New Year!" at midnight. Many places have big fireworks shows.

description: Celebrated on the birthday of Louis Braille (1809–1852), who invented the Braille system — a way of reading and writing using raised dots that blind people can feel with their fingers.
why_special: Before Braille, blind people had very few ways to read and write. Louis Braille's invention gave them independence and access to knowledge. How does Braille work? Each letter is made of a pattern of 6 dots (2 columns of 3 dots). By feeling the pattern, blind people can read books, write letters, and even use computers!
facts: Louis Braille invented this system when he was just 15 years old! He himself became blind at age 3 after an accident in his father's workshop. His invention has helped millions of blind people worldwide.

description: The day the Constitution of India came into effect on 26 January 1950, making India a Republic (a country where the head of state is elected, not a king).
why_special: Before 1950, India was ruled by the British. After independence (1947), India needed its own set of laws — the Constitution. It was drafted by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and adopted on 26 November 1949, but came into effect on 26 January 1950. On 26 January 1930, the Indian National Congress declared Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) at the Lahore session. So, 26 January was chosen to honour that declaration.
how_celebrated: A grand parade is held at Rajpath (now Kartavya Path) in New Delhi. It showcases: Military power — tanks, missiles, fighter jets; Cultural floats — from every state of India; Marching contingents — Army, Navy, Air Force, police; Fly-past — Indian Air Force jets with tricolour smoke; The President hoists the flag and gives a speech. The National Anthem "Jana Gana Mana" is sung.
facts: The Constitution is the longest written constitution of any country in the world (448 articles, 12 schedules).
It took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to draft.
The original Constitution is written in both Hindi and English and is kept in a special helium-filled case in the Parliament.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the first President of India on this day.

Ramanujan died at the young age of 32.
His work is still used in physics, cryptography, and computer science today.
